Team — quick technical readout:

- Initial telemetry shows tail-latency increase concentrated on model-v2 routing nodes; CPU on those pods is normal but we see a sustained queue depth rise and higher I/O wait on NVMe on two hosts.
- Error signatures are timeouts between the routing proxy and the KV cache tier (~503 from cache timeouts).

Immediate mitigation actions I'm recommending (in flight):
1) Toggle routing to model-v1 (compatible fallback) for the affected workload (will reduce accuracy but cuts token length and latency). ETA: 12m.
2) Evict and reprovision the two suspect hosts (in parallel) — SRE running. ETA: 40–60m.
3) Rate-limit background batch jobs hitting the cache to relieve pressure — 8m.

I will push the routing toggle first and monitor p95/p99. Laura

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-20 14:12 -0800
Subject: Post-mitigations telemetry & preliminary root cause

Team / Alex — post-mitigation signal and preliminary RCA: 

- Timeline: routing toggle to model-v1 at 2026-11-19T09:58 PT removed the immediate latency spike (p95 dropped from ~1.6s to ~320ms). Full host reprovision and cache warm completed by 2026-11-19T12:42 PT. Error rate fell to <0.2%.
- Root cause: a staged background batch deployed on our internal cache tier unexpectedly increased scan frequency and triggered LRU thrashing on two hosts. The scanning job had a config drift (concurrency=24 vs intended 6).
- Corrective actions taken:
  * Rolled back the batch to the previous concurrency setting and applied a config guard (feature flag + a pre-deploy check).
  * Added telemetry alerts for cache queue depth and NVMe i/o wait spikes.
  * Emergency canary policy: route-time fallback to stable model variants now automated when cache timeouts exceed threshold.

Attachments: slo-delta-graph-11-20.png (SLO impact graph), postmortem-draft.md (internal).

We'll prepare a short customer-facing post-mortem and an updated MAP with concrete credits and timeline.

— David
Director, Telemetry & Reliability
